claims: The Iran nuclear agreement is formally known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).
JCPOA was a 2015 accord reached between Iran and the P5+1 (the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, China, and Germany) plus the European Union.
JCPOA was negotiated under the Obama administration.
Iran agreed to limit its uranium enrichment to 3.67% for 15 years.
90% uranium enrichment is required for weapons-grade material.
Iran agreed to reduce its enriched uranium stockpile by 98% (down to 300 kg) for 15 years.
The number of operating centrifuges at the Natanz facility was capped at 5,060 for ten years.
The number of operating centrifuges at the Natanz facility was down from nearly 20,000.
The Fordow facility was converted into a nuclear physics center rather than an enrichment site.
The Arak heavy-water reactor was redesigned to prevent the production of weapons-grade plutonium.
The IAEA was granted extensive long-term monitoring access to Iran's nuclear facilities.
IAEA monitoring included supply chain oversight.
The IAEA had the ability to request access to suspicious undeclared sites within 24 days.
The IAEA verified that Iran had complied with JCPOA steps on January 16, 2016.
The U.S., EU, and UN lifted nuclear-related sanctions following IAEA verification on January 16, 2016.
Sanctions relief allowed Iran to access over $100 billion in frozen assets.
A major goal of the JCPOA was to increase Iran's breakout time from approximately 2-3 months to at least one year.
Breakout time is the time required to produce enough weapons-grade material for one nuclear weapon.
President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from the JCPOA in 2018.
President Donald Trump called the JCPOA a 'horrible, one-sided deal'.
President Donald Trump initiated a 'maximum pressure' campaign.
President Donald Trump reimposed sanctions.
Iran began violating the JCPOA restrictions in retaliation to the U.S. withdrawal.
Iran increased its uranium enrichment to 60%.
Iran reduced its cooperation with IAEA inspectors.
The Biden administration has sought to revive the JCPOA.
As of late 2023, many provisions of the JCPOA have started to expire.
